headline: Bitcoin is holding near $60,000 on Sunday after Saturday's crash to a two-year low, with fear still extreme and a short US holiday week full of data ahead.

market.asOf: Prices from CoinMarketCap coin pages, read by this desk at about 11:52-11:54 UTC on Sun 22 Nov (18:53 Bangkok). Other price sites showed different 24h changes, so treat those as rough. Prices move fast; use the live prices on this page.
market.fearGreed: 12 out of 100, "Extreme Fear", on the Alternative.me Crypto Fear & Greed Index (read at about 11:51 UTC), the same as the day before and 13 a week ago.

stories.title: Bitcoin steadies near $60,000 after crashing to a two-year low
stories.summary: Bitcoin fell to its lowest price since September 2024 on Saturday, then bounced more than 9% back above $60,000. On Sunday it has moved sideways, but it is still about 12% lower than a week ago, and many short-term holders sent coins to exchanges at a loss.
points: Bitcoin fell as low as $55,130, its lowest since September 2024, then rose more than 9% to about $60,300, per CoinDesk.
Bitcoin was about $60,424 on Sunday morning, down 12.53% on the week, with the whole crypto market worth about $2.03 trillion, per crypto.news.

Forced selling of leveraged bets totalled about $1.8 billion over 24 hours, $1.3 billion of it from bets on higher prices, per CoinDesk citing CoinGlass; crypto.news cites the Kobeissi Letter at about $2.7 billion.
Short-term holders sent 92,100 BTC (about $5.34 billion) to exchanges at a loss on 21 Nov, per crypto.news citing CryptoQuant.
CoinDesk says traders see Monday's US stock open as the next test of the bounce.

sources.label: crypto.news: bitcoin rebounds from $55K after big liquidations

stories.title: US bitcoin funds lose about $1.25 billion for a third straight $1 billion week
stories.summary: Money kept leaving US spot bitcoin ETFs, the funds that let people buy bitcoin through a normal brokerage account. It is the third week in a row of outflows above $1 billion, and BlackRock's fund had its worst day ever on Thursday.
points: Bitcoin ETFs lost $1.25 billion over 16-20 Nov and ether ETFs $221.7 million, per crypto.news using Farside data; Incrypted, using SoSoValue, put the bitcoin figure at $1.24 billion.
Incrypted says it is the third straight week above $1 billion, with more than $3.59 billion out over the three weeks.
On Thursday 19 Nov BlackRock's IBIT lost $541.1 million, its biggest daily outflow since launch, per CEO Economy.
Friday's total was -$124.5 million with IBIT's figure still blank on Farside, per crypto.news.

sources.label: crypto.news: bitcoin and ether ETF outflows, 16-20 Nov
Incrypted: $3.59 billion out over three weeks

stories.title: Inflation data, a likely Fed hike and a big options expiry crowd a short holiday week
stories.summary: Traders widely expect the Fed to raise rates again in December, so Wednesday's US inflation data matters more than usual. US markets close Thursday for Thanksgiving, and a large batch of bitcoin options expires Friday.
points: October PCE inflation and Q3 GDP are both due Wed 25 Nov; core PCE is expected at 3.2% a year against 3.1% before, per Newsquawk.

Rate-hike odds have slipped during the stock sell-off: 24/7 Wall St put the chance of a quarter-point December hike at about 92% on 21 Nov, against 95.7% in CME FedWatch on 19 Nov per Seoul Economic Daily.
Bitcoin options covering 112,323 BTC, about $6.76 billion, expire on Deribit on Fri 27 Nov at 08:00 UTC, per Cryptoticker (Deribit data from 21 Nov).
The Nasdaq fell more than 4% on Friday, per CoinDesk.

sources.label: 24/7 Wall St: selloff could block Fed hikes
Seoul Economic Daily: December rate hike odds

briefs.title: Bitcoin briefly prints near $17,000 on Kraken's Canadian-dollar market
briefs.summary: Bitcoin traded as low as C$24,250 (about $16,900) on Kraken's BTC/CAD market during the sell-off; Kraken found no security breach and says executed trades stand, per Cointelegraph.

briefs.title: Chainflip hack put at about $12 million
briefs.summary: The loss includes 122.86 BTC, 520.22 ETH, 3.25 million USDC and 758,141 USDT, up from a first estimate of $4.86 million; Chainflip offers the attacker 10% if 90% is returned by 18:38 UTC on Mon 23 Nov, per Cointelegraph.

briefs.title: Kalshi faces a Monday court hearing in New York
briefs.summary: A Manhattan state court hears New York Attorney General Letitia James's request for a restraining order on Mon 23 Nov at 11:30am ET; Kalshi says it would shut its exchange nationwide, the AG's office says that is not its aim, per The Block.

briefs.title: Bitcoin miner earnings hit a record low
briefs.summary: Hashprice, what miners earn per unit of computing power, fell to about $26.20 per PH/s per day on 21 Nov, the lowest in DC Forecasts' data back to 2015, and a mining difficulty rise of about 9.4% is projected around 27 Nov.

briefs.title: Strategy leaves MSCI indexes at the end of November
briefs.summary: Strategy is removed from the MSCI USA, World and ACWI indexes at the close of 30 Nov; MSCI-linked funds held about 13 million of its shares, per 24/7 Wall St.

briefs.title: BTCS warns of liquidation risk on its Aave loan
briefs.summary: The Nasdaq-listed company had about $54 million of ether-backed Aave debt as of 19 Nov and warned the collateral could be liquidated if prices fall further, per The Defiant.

briefs.title: Cyber bridge exploit; Upbit and Bithumb freeze CYBER transfers
briefs.summary: Cyber detected unexpected minting of CYBER tokens on Solana and told users not to use its bridge or deposit CYBER to exchanges; Bithumb and Upbit suspended deposits and withdrawals, per Cointelegraph.

briefs.title: SEC charges eight firms over fake crypto platforms
briefs.summary: The SEC says the schemes took about $37.4 million from more than 1,500 US investors using fake certificates, social-media ads and private chat groups, per Cointelegraph. A reminder to check any platform before sending money.

calendar.event: Token unlocks: SOON, MON, SOSO, XPL, H, HUMA, SIGN, PROS, GRASS, FF, CARDS
calendar.note: SOON on Monday 23, MON (the largest, about 16.6 billion tokens worth about $220M on this desk's data) and SOSO on Tuesday 24, XPL and H on Wednesday 25, HUMA on Thursday 26, SIGN, PROS and GRASS on Saturday 28, and FF and CARDS on Sunday 29 November. See the unlock table on this page for sizes, dates and confidence. (Dates from this desk's unlock data.)
The previous readings were 54.9 for manufacturing and 56.1 for services, per LiteFinance.

calendar.event: New York court hearing on Kalshi
calendar.note: Justice Melissa Crane hears the New York Attorney General's request for a restraining order; Kalshi says it would shut its exchange nationwide, per The Block.

calendar.event: New York Fed President John Williams speaks
calendar.note: Remarks on the economic outlook and monetary policy, followed by Q&A, per the New York Fed.
Expected at 92.5, per The Rio Times, after 91.7 in October.
Both report on Tue 24 Nov; Workday's call is at 4:30pm ET (04:30 Bangkok) and HP's at 5:00pm ET (05:00 Bangkok), per the companies.

calendar.event: US PCE inflation (Oct), Q3 GDP (second estimate), durable goods and jobless claims
calendar.note: Core PCE is expected at 3.2% a year (prior 3.1%), per Newsquawk. Q3 GDP is expected at 3.5% against the 3.4% first estimate, per Economic Weekly. Weekly jobless claims come out on Wednesday this week because of Thanksgiving; the last reading was 203K, per Newsquawk.
The Fed's survey of business conditions around the country, per Economic Weekly. October new home sales come out earlier the same day at 10:00am ET (22:00 Bangkok), per Economic Weekly.
On Friday 27 Nov US stocks close early at 1:00pm ET (01:00 Sat Bangkok), per NYSE. Crypto trades all day, but thin trading can mean bigger swings.

calendar.event: Monthly bitcoin options expiry on Deribit
calendar.note: About $6.76 billion of bitcoin options (112,323 BTC) expire, with the "max pain" level at $73,000, per Cryptoticker using Deribit data from 21 Nov.
The last jobs report before the Fed decision, per the BLS schedule. November CPI is Thu 10 Dec, the day after the Fed decision, per the BLS.

calendar.event: Next Fed meeting and rate decision
calendar.note: Two-day meeting 8-9 Dec; the decision is at 2:00pm ET on Wed 9 Dec (02:00 Thu Bangkok), per the Fed. Fed officials stop public comment on policy from Sat 28 Nov, under the Fed's blackout rule (from the second Saturday before a meeting). 24/7 Wall St put the chance of a quarter-point hike at about 92% on 21 Nov.
